case.label: B
case.text: Create a read replica in a second AZ: a replica can be promoted if the AZ fails and also takes the reports; weak because promotion is manual and asynchronous replication may lose committed data.

case.label: D
case.text: Roll back in place keeps the endpoint; weak because RDS point-in-time restore always creates a new DB instance.

case.label: B
case.text: Retry logic plus a short DNS TTL is the classic fix and adds no new service; weak because the stem accepts only minimal code changes and B touches every component.

case.label: A
case.text: Create the replica from a manual snapshot; weak because the block is the zero retention period, not a missing snapshot.

case.label: C
case.text: Multi-AZ standby could take the reports; weak because the standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance does not serve reads.

case.label: D
case.text: A same-AZ replica gives a failover target; weak because it is in the failed AZ and promotion is manual.

case.label: A
case.text: Multi-AZ DB instance gives sub-minute failover and a standby; weak because that standby does not serve reads.

case.label: B
case.text: Point-in-time restore gives a copy; weak because it is a new instance limited to the retention window and does not keep a copy for 7 years.

case.label: A
case.text: Larger gp2 grows baseline IOPS; weak because gp2 does not give the lowest or most consistent latency. The stem names a general-purpose instance class and option C does not say whether io2 Block Express needs another class.

case.label: A
case.text: DMS keeps a synced copy and allows a cutover; weak because it needs a task, endpoints and schema work that Blue/Green avoids.

case.label: B
case.text: B has no daily manual step and saves weekend cost; weak because it pays for idle weeknights, so C costs less.

case.label: C
case.text: A proxy pools connections and could help any database; weak because it adds cost and a network hop for a workload already pooled.

case.label: B
case.text: A replica takes read load; weak because the failure is connection count from Lambda, which a replica does not pool.

case.label: A
case.text: Dump and restore into a new encrypted instance works; weak because it is more scripted work than snapshot copy and restore.

case.label: A
case.text: Plain RDS for SQL Server is cheaper to operate; weak because RDS gives no operating system access for an agent.

case.label: B
case.text: Reusing the us-east-1 key ARN for the replica; weak because KMS keys are Regional so the replica needs a key in us-west-2.

answers.flag: The stem asks for a copy of each day's backup, but options A and E describe one-time steps and none names a daily automation, so a careful candidate could say the stem lacks the automation constraint or that no listed pair fully meets it.

case.label: D
case.text: Share the automated snapshot directly; weak because automated snapshots cannot be shared and an aws/rds-encrypted snapshot cannot be shared either.

case.label: A
case.text: ElastiCache cuts repeated reads; weak because it needs application code changes and is less efficient than more memory for the buffer cache.

case.label: A
case.text: Alarm plus Lambda also adds storage on demand; weak because it is custom code to maintain, so more overhead than storage autoscaling.

case.label: C
case.text: Automated backups can be retained after deletion; weak because they expire with the retention period of 7 days, not 2 years.

case.label: C
case.text: Multi-AZ standby shares query load; weak because the standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance does not serve reads.

case.label: D
case.text: A change-copy job gives a writable reporting copy; weak because it is far more development effort than a MySQL replica with read_only set to 0.
